things.name: Salt
things.say: Table salt is a chemical called sodium chloride. It is made of two elements, sodium and chlorine, joined together. Each tiny grain is shaped like a little cube.

box.title: Not all salt looks the same
box.say: Sea salt and pink salt are still mostly sodium chloride. They also have tiny amounts of other minerals. Pink salt gets its colour from a little iron, and sea salt has a little magnesium and calcium from the sea.

things.name: Sugar
things.say: Sugar is a chemical called sucrose. It is made of carbon, hydrogen and oxygen. Plants like sugar cane make sugar using sunlight.

things.name: Water
things.say: Water is made of hydrogen and oxygen. Each tiny piece of water has two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom. That is why water is called H two O.

things.name: Baking soda
things.say: Baking soda is a chemical called sodium bicarbonate. When it meets something sour, like vinegar or lemon juice, it fizzes and makes bubbles of a gas called carbon dioxide.

box.title: Fizz with a grown-up
box.say: Put a spoon of baking soda in a cup and add a little vinegar. The bubbles are carbon dioxide gas. Bubbles like these help some cakes rise and get fluffy.

things.name: Vinegar
things.say: Vinegar is mostly water with a little acetic acid mixed in. The acid is what makes vinegar taste sour.

things.name: Lemon
things.say: Lemons taste sour because they have citric acid inside. Oranges and limes have citric acid too.

box.title: Sour means acid
box.say: Sour foods, like lemons and vinegar, have acids in them. The acids in lemons and vinegar are made of carbon, hydrogen and oxygen, the same elements as sugar, but joined in a different way.

things.name: Kitchen foil
things.say: Kitchen foil is a thin sheet of aluminium. Aluminium is a metal, element number thirteen. It is light and easy to bend.

things.name: Steel pot
things.say: A steel pot is made mostly of iron with a little carbon. Stainless steel also has chromium in it, and the chromium helps stop the pot from rusting.

things.name: Milk
things.say: Milk has calcium in it. Calcium is a metal element, and our bodies use it to build strong bones and teeth.
